title: LGB+: A Macroeconomic Forecasting Road Test
hypothesis: LGB+ family interleaves greedy univariate linear updates (selected by max|Corr| with residuals from random feature subset, fitted by OLS) with shallow tree updates in single boosting loop, with per-step OOB competition (LGB+) or deterministic alternating schedule T trees +1 linear (LGBA+); final prediction additive linear+tree sum allows decomposition into linear/nonlinear contributions for forecasts, permutation VI into linear/trees/cross-term, and dual observation weights w_lin+w_tree; delivers gains where linear autoregressive persistence or near-accounting linear links dominate (especially short-horizon UR, IP, housing) while remaining robust across linear to highly nonlinear DGPs, whereas pure tree methods expend capacity approximating linear structure inefficiently in small macro samples.
data_sources: Estimation and forecasting use FRED-QD (Federal Reserve Economic Database Quarterly, McCracken-Ng 2020) transformed to stationarity; MARX augmentation (Goulet Coulombe et al. 2024 transformation) with MA 2,4,8; Survey of Professional Forecasters (SPF) median from Philadelphia Fed (Stark 2010, Engelberg et al. 2022 Manskie) for CPI inflation, GDP growth, housing starts, unemployment, industrial production - no SPF for Delta Spread; NBER recession dates shading in figures; simulation synthetic data as defined in Appendix Simulation Design.
sample: U.S. quarterly macro forecasting exercise: six targets (headline CPI inflation, GDP growth, unemployment rate, housing starts log growth, industrial production, term spread 10Y-3M [Delta Spread] ) using FRED-QD database predictors transformed to stationarity, augmented with 4 lags + MARX moving averages orders 2,4,8, plus 4 PCs with 4 lags each, standardized over training sample, 37 slowly released variables shifted forward 1 quarter for ragged edge. Direct forecasts h=1,2,4 with separate models per horizon. Expanding window re-estimated every 8 quarters from 1961Q2 training start. Out-of-sample evaluation split pre-COVID 2007Q2--2019Q4 (51 quarters) and post-COVID 2022Q1--2025Q1 for GDP/UR/IP and 2021Q1--2025Q1 for inflation/housing/DSpread (13 or 17 quarters) as printed. Models compared: AR(4) benchmark (=1.00 denominator), FAAR, RR, KRR, RF (500 trees), LightGBM, LGB+ competition with OOB selection + post-hoc calibration y=beta*hat y no intercept, LGBA+ alternating with T in 5-20 and eta_lin <= eta_tree, NN/HNN (inflation only), TabPFN, SPF median (CPI,GDP,housing,unemployment, IP). No subgroup sample-size counts printed beyond window dates; counts not stated are not claims. Replication sample must use exact variables, transforms, horizons and windows as above. Full RMSE relative to AR reported for 18 variable-horizon rows x 8 models x 2 periods = 288 cells in Table 1; representative headline subset listed in claims. Simulation auxiliary sample: P=6 uniform[0,1], 8 DGPs with f(x) definitions in Appendix, SNR {0.5,1,2}, N {250,500,1000}, Ntest=1000, 10 replications - method parameters only, not empirical claims. Dual interpretation sample: same expanding-window training data portfolio producing AXIL weights w_ji per training observation i for forecast j, smoothed 4Q centered MA, decomposed w_lin+w_tree, illustrated for three forecast dates (UR 2009Q2, DSpread 2024Q4, HOUST 2022Q3) with top window/quarter weights printed above.
method: 1. Data construction: take FRED-QD quarterly vintages (McCracken 2020), apply standard stationarity transformations (log diff where needed), then MARX augmentation: for each series add 4 lags plus moving averages orders 2,4,8; extract first 4 principal components from transformed panel and add 4 lags each; standardize all series to zero mean/unit variance over training sample only; shift 37 slowly released variables (output, productivity, compensation, Fed balance sheet) forward 1 quarter to respect publication lag.

2. Model suite specification as in Appendix Models: AR(4) benchmark; FAAR (4 lags target + 2 lags of 4 PCs); Ridge RR (CV lambda); KRR (Gaussian/Laplacian kernels CV sigma/lambda); RF 500 trees 75% row subsampling min node 5 random feature subsets; LightGBM histogram boosting CV learning rate/depth/sampling with early stopping; NN 3x400 ReLU dropout0.2 Adam early stopping; HNN for inflation only (hemisphere architecture); TabPFN single forward pass in-context; SPF Philadelphia Fed median; LGB+ (Algorithm 1): initialize F0=mean y, for t=1..M draw subsample St size floor(qN), compute residuals r=y-F_{t-1} on St, candidate tree ht fit to residuals -> Ftree=F_{t-1}+eta ht, candidate linear: sample feature subset Jt size floor(rho P), select k*=argmax|Corr(X_k,r)| on St, fit univariate OLS r=alpha+beta X_{k*} on St -> Flin=F_{t-1}+eta*(alpha+beta X_{k*}), evaluate L_tree and L_lin on judge set (OOB = complement of St, recommended for macro) and set Ft to winner; ensembling average small number independent runs; post-hoc calibration for LGB+ only per expanding window: regress y in-sample on fitted y without intercept (y=beta*haty) estimate beta on training fitted values and multiply out-of-sample predictions for that window - recursive, no lookahead.

3. Alternating variant LGBA+ (Algorithm 2, Section 2.2): for m=1..M cycles compute residuals r, fit T trees sequentially {ht} t=1..T to residuals -> tildeF=F_{m-1}+eta_tree sum ht, then compute residuals rprime=y-tildeF, select k*=argmax_k|Corr(X_k,rprime)| over all P (no rho), fit OLS rprime=alpha+beta X_{k*} -> Fm=tildeF+eta_lin*(alpha+beta X_{k*}); hyperparameters T in [5,20] and eta_lin <= eta_tree are free; no OOB per-step evaluation; removes rho hyperparameter.

4. Forecasting: estimate direct h-step models h=1,2,4 separately for each target on expanding window starting 1961Q2, re-estimated every 8 quarters, produce out-of-sample forecasts for evaluation windows 2007Q2--2019Q4 pre-COVID and post-COVID 2022Q1--2025Q1 (GDP/UR/IP) or 2021Q1--2025Q1 (inflation/housing/DSpread) per Table 1 note; compute error e_t = y_{t+h}-hat y_{t+h|t}; classical metrics RMSE and MAE reported relative to AR RMSE (=RMSE_model/RMSE_AR so AR=1.00) per Table 1, plus DM t-stat = mean loss differential / HAC SE vs AR, rho1 = first-order autocorrelation of errors, and risk-adjusted metrics (Return Sharpe Sortino Omega MaxDD Edge) per appendix tables Panels A-C (not headline). Best = bold green, second-best = bold as marked.

5. Interpretability decomposition: for each forecast write additive prediction hat y = f_lin(X)+f_tree(X) by regrouping linear OLS updates and tree updates; plot stacked shaded regions over time (Fig dashboards). Variable importance: for each variable group g (all lags/MARX of same underlying series) randomly permute values across evaluation period, recompute predictions, VI_g = (MSE_permuted - MSE_baseline)/MSE_baseline *100. Channel decomposition: permute only in linear channel to get VI_lin, only in tree channel to get VI_trees, both channels gives VI=VI_lin+VI_trees+C_g where C_g=200/(n MSE_base) sum_i Delta_lin_i * Delta_tree_i (synergy cross-term); display teal linear/red trees/gray cross-term. Paper notes decomposition indicative (trees may still capture some linear). No p-values, number of permutations or confidence intervals printed - not stated.

6. Dual interpretation (Section 3.2, Geertsema 2023 AXIL/Goulet 2024 dual): for LGBA+ only (implemented) express out-of-sample forecast as weighted average of training outcomes hat y_j = w_j y = sum_i w_ji y_i with w_ji = w^lin_ji + w^tree_ji via additive decomposition; smooth weights with 4-quarter centered MA; report top individual quarters and top 4-quarter windows with decomposed teal/red contributions for selected dates 2009Q2 (UR trough), 2024Q4 (DSpread steepening), 2022Q3 (Housing rate shock) with weights as listed in claims; COVID quarters 2020Q1--2021Q2 excluded (zero weight) for DSpread example; historical narrative percentages (e.g., 60% 1983 rebound) illustrative not estimated by model.

7. Simulation cross-check (Section 2.3, Appendix A): generate 8 DGPs definitions (Linear; Product-Log; Mixture = 2x1+1.5x2 + 3sin pi x3x4+2(x5-0.5)^2 equal variance; Friedman1 10sin pi x1x2+20(x3-0.5)^2+10x4+5x5; Trig-Log sin pi sum+log1+x4^2; Soft Radial 1/(1+5||x-0.5||^2); Step/U-curve mixture of indicators + quadratics; Rotated Sine sin3 sum) with P=6 uniform[0,1], y=f(x)+N(0,sigma^2) calibrated to SNR 0.5,1,2, N=250,500,1000 training, Ntest=1000 fixed, 10 replications; compute out-of-sample R2 per configuration averaged over replications; display Figure simulation_stacked Panels A (SNR0.5 avg over N), B (N250 avg over SNR), C (N1000 avg over SNR) +/-1 SD error bars and Table simulation_results detailed numbers; text conclusions: LGB+ trails OLS least under pure linear, only beats OLS in small-sample low-SNR Mixture, does not hurt under highly nonlinear (coeffs hover 0, diversified selection), RF best under extremely nonlinear Rotated Sine.

8. No ex ante variable selection for linear channel - built incrementally during training; linear and tree components jointly optimized in one loop; contrast to two-stage residualization or pre-commitment partially linear/local linear forests.
